purpose: S4 for batch 5, the last: the first-public minute of each release in the fifth batch, taken from the public wire page, and what was found on the way. config/m5-phase1b-events.json now holds five events built from it in the dry-run state after the thirty-eight of batches 1 to 4: sealed, no attestations, so each quarantines on FIRST_PUBLIC_TIME_UNVERIFIED until the owner attests it. None was made at the bell. Nothing here is a price, a return or a label.

permission.read_as: Batch 5 only: the public pages of the releases of the five candidates listed below on Business Wire, GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire or Accesswire, or on the issuer's own newsroom, to take each release's first-public minute, and a check for a separate same-day release. In the built-in browser, in browser memory only; the URL, the displayed minute and a short excerpt are kept. No web-search tool, no price or quote page, no filing. It carries no push and no other download. It is the last batch: the final audit (S7) needs no pages.

reading.what: The five releases' pages and company searches on GlobeNewswire and Business Wire (each issuer's wire is the one its earlier events in the repository used); held in browser memory only; the URL, the displayed minute, the page's machine-readable time and the same-day check results are kept. Business Wire's two release pages were loaded a second time to read the date and time the page itself displays, which the first extraction (the page's machine-readable time) had not given. No filing was opened: EDGAR's acceptance times come from the archived SEC lists already in the repository. Listings were read through short extractions of the dates, times and titles wanted, so as to see as little else as possible.
reading.what_was_seen_in_passing: Business Wire's Sanfilippo listing returned the opening sentences of the 2026-08-19 release (net sales, sales volume, gross profit and diluted earnings per share for its fiscal fourth quarter); the dateline extraction of Okta's release page included the end of a bullet before the dateline ('... cash flow of $227 million'); Okta's phrase-search listing showed the titles and times of its releases from 2026-05-21 to 2026-09-18, including two after its results (2026-09-14, a webcast notice, and 2026-09-18, a board appointment). These are company-reported business content, not a price, a return or a label of any event.
reading.refused_or_missing: No site refused a page for permission, and Business Wire answered every request: I made one search at a time, with release pages between them. The first Business Wire search page re-navigated by itself once while my first script ran, so that script was cut off and the extraction was redone on the loaded page; the first batch call (GlobeNewswire's Rekor search) stopped at its first action because the pane had to be opened, but that page had loaded and was read without a second load.

Not a proof that nothing earlier was public: open-web research can show no discoverable earlier disclosure, not a negative.
Not a price, a return or a label of any event: none was read; the sealed run prints none.
